relations.summary: Confirmation-bias blocks active-listening when incoming information is filtered to support what the listener already wants to believe.
Active-listening conflicts with confirmation-bias when the listener processes incoming information to confirm existing assumptions rather than genuinely absorbing the speaker's meaning.
Confirmation-bias blocks adaptation when new signals are interpreted to defend the current path instead of changing it.
Adaptation conflicts with confirmation-bias when feedback is interpreted to confirm the current path rather than trigger revision.
Adverse-selection conflicts with confirmation-bias when screeners overweight the signals that fit their prior beliefs about quality.
Confirmation-bias turns agile-methodologies into ritualized hypothesis protection by using sprints to confirm a favored conclusion.
Agile-methodologies conflicts with confirmation-bias when hypothesis-driven sprints are used to confirm a mandated conclusion rather than genuinely test it.
Confirmation-bias prevents aleatory-epistemic-uncertainty-recognition from updating ignorance honestly because disconfirming evidence never changes the uncertainty map.

Aleatory-epistemic-uncertainty-recognition conflicts with confirmation-bias when the tendency to confirm existing beliefs prevents recognition of disconfirming evidence needed to reduce epistemic ignorance.
Confirmation-bias can get baked into the procedure when the algorithm is designed to confirm the designer's prior model rather than test it against hard cases.
Algorithmic-thinking conflicts with confirmation-bias when procedure design embeds assumptions that confirm the designer's prior model rather than testing it against edge cases.
Confirmation-bias makes antifragility brittle because it resists learning from disorder that contradicts the current model.
Confirmation-bias makes association dangerous when it reinforces the first preferred pattern instead of testing alternatives.
Association conflicts with confirmation-bias when associative links are selectively activated to reinforce a pre-existing narrative rather than tested against disconfirming evidence.
Confirmation-bias corrupts auditability-traceability when the trail is built to justify a wanted answer instead of to expose how the judgment really formed.
Confirmation-bias undermines authenticity when people defend a preferred self-story instead of facing uncomfortable truth.
Authenticity conflicts with confirmation-bias when commitment to one's authentic position becomes selective attention to supporting evidence.
Authority-bias conflicts with confirmation-bias when deference to the expert selectively amplifies confirming evidence.
Base-rates conflicts with confirmation-bias when prior beliefs override inconvenient outside-view frequencies.
Baseline-establishment conflicts with confirmation-bias when evidence is filtered to preserve the existing baseline instead of honestly challenging whether it still reflects reality.
Batna conflicts with confirmation-bias when negotiators assess the current deal and the walk-away alternative selectively rather than honestly.
Confirmation-bias blocks bayesian updating by filtering evidence so the posterior never honestly moves.
Bayesian conflicts with confirmation-bias when posterior updates are blocked by selective evidence acceptance.
Confirmation-bias is reinforced by bias-blind-spot when self-unaware reasoning seeks support for existing conclusions while overlooking disconfirming information.
Bias-blind-spot conflicts with confirmation-bias when self-unaware reasoning reinforces the preferred conclusion while treating disconfirming evidence as less real.
Confirmation-bias undermines blooms-taxonomy by distorting the impartial analysis and evaluation needed before strong judgment or synthesis can be trusted.
Bottlenecks conflicts with confirmation-bias when teams protect the chosen constraint diagnosis instead of testing alternate system limiters.
Brainstorming conflicts with confirmation-bias when evaluation during generation selectively develops only ideas that confirm the group's existing direction.
Calculated-risk-taking conflicts with confirmation-bias when risk estimates are calibrated to justify a preferred course of action rather than derived from independent evidence.
Confirmation-bias distorts category-decisions when the bucket is defended for political comfort instead of evidence.
Confirmation-bias undermines causal-attribution-resistance by locking onto the first plausible culprit and selectively reading later evidence through that story.
Causal-attribution-resistance conflicts with confirmation-bias when early blame stories are defended instead of reopened as causal evidence accumulates.
Confirmation-bias pressures chain-of-verification to validate the preferred story rather than reconcile disconfirming evidence link by link.
Chain-of-verification conflicts with confirmation-bias when each verification step unconsciously confirms prior steps rather than genuinely testing them for disconfirmation.
Confirmation-bias makes circle-of-competence count only the evidence that flatters the current boundary story.

Circle-of-competence conflicts with confirmation-bias when practitioners selectively count successes to confirm they are operating inside their competence circle rather than honestly mapping its edges.

Confirmation bias is one of cognitive dissonance's primary resolution tools — seeking out confirming evidence and minimizing disconfirming evidence reduces the dissonance that would arise if contradictory evidence were weighted honestly.

Cognitive-gaps-assessment conflicts with confirmation-bias when assessments overweight already-favored capability narratives.
